statements.quote: Join the us on Sunday in NYC at Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment!
statements.context: Closing line of the post (dated 2024-05-01). The author invites readers to his RAMHT (Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment) live event on Sunday in New York City. Implicit claim that the event takes place as scheduled.
statements.note: Event announcement about the author's own RAMHT series; weak predictive content.

statements.quote: Change healthcare was Cyber attacked. And, as I predicted, the entire company had to be scrapped.
statements.context: Opening of a post on UnitedHealth CEO Andrew Witty's congressional testimony about the Change Healthcare cyberattack. The author says he predicted that Change Healthcare would have to be scrapped and rebuilt from scratch, and that this has now happened.
statements.note: Restatement of an earlier call that the author says has resolved; not forward-looking at the post date.

statements.quote: If they didn't have endless money for lawyers, more than the everyone who will sue them
statements.context: After describing UnitedHealth/Change Healthcare's failure to enforce its own two-factor authentication policy, the author implies that many parties will sue them, and that UnitedHealth's legal resources will shield it from consequences.
statements.note: Incomplete sentence (trails off); implied forecast of lawsuits against UnitedHealth over the Change breach.

statements.quote: Reminder— this Sunday, May 5th, I have a Frontier Psychiatrists Live Event… Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment 2024 NYC.
statements.context: Closing reminder in a post about Osmind and the APA DSM-5-TR Level 1 Cross-Cutting Measure. The author announces his RAMHT 2024 NYC live event for Sunday, May 5th, 2024.
statements.note: Event announcement about the author's own RAMHT series; weak predictive content.

statements.quote: It's not all NFTs and psychedelics that are still illegal but will change everything, we promise!
statements.context: Post on Tim Ferriss bringing accelerated TMS to the SXSW stage. The author sarcastically voices the conference's recurring hype that still-illegal psychedelics will change everything, contrasting it with aTMS as an actually disruptive technology.
statements.note: Sarcastic voicing of SXSW hype; the author mocks the forecast rather than making it.

statements.quote: the Nobel prize in waiting science of Nolan Williams’ Brain Simulation lab at Stanford
statements.context: The author describes the accelerated TMS science from Nolan Williams's Stanford Brain Stimulation Lab, discussed by Tim Ferriss at SXSW, as 'Nobel prize in waiting', implying it will eventually win a Nobel prize.
statements.note: Hyperbolic praise with an implicit Nobel prize forecast; no date.

statements.quote: I’m a serial killer for “the mental health crisis.” Only the article—“The”—will be left standing by the end.
statements.context: Mission statement post explaining the newsletter's purpose. The author says he intends to dismantle the whole phrase 'the mental health crisis' word by word in his writing, so that only 'The' remains by the end.
statements.note: Statement of intent about the newsletter's own framing; rhetorical, weak predictive content.

statements.quote: Mental health is a nonsense phrase, and I will dispense with it as useful.
statements.context: Same mission statement post. The author declares he will stop treating the phrase 'mental health' as useful in the newsletter.
statements.note: Statement of intent about the author's own usage; weak predictive content.

statements.quote: This newsletter strives to address both of these issues—we define mental health problems, and we will examine how brains and minds can conspire with the outside world to drive behavior over the edge for vulnerable people.
statements.context: Same mission statement post. The author lays out the newsletter's future editorial plan: define mental health problems and examine how brains, minds and environment drive behavior in vulnerable people.
statements.note: Editorial plan for the newsletter; a plan rather than a forecast about the world.

statements.quote: He will maintain his position through the end of June. DeathStance’s Human CEO, Kevin Burns, said he does not have immediate plans to replace him.
statements.context: Satirical report on the Q1 earnings call of 'DeathStance Health, Inc. (Nasdaq: VAMP)', an apparent parody of LifeStance Health. 'Dracula', president and chief vampiric officer, announces his resignation; he stays through the end of June and the CEO has no immediate plans to replace him.
statements.note: Satire; executive transition timeline attributed to fictional characters, likely mirroring a real executive departure.

statements.quote: The company raised its center margin expectations from 352 million to 372 million liters, and adjusted BBITDA expectations from 87 to 99 million liters.
statements.context: Same satirical earnings-call report. The fictional company raises its full-year guidance for center margin (352 to 372 million) and adjusted EBITDA ('BBITDA', 87 to 99 million), rendered in liters of blood.
statements.note: Satire; guidance raise attributed to the parodied company's leadership, apparently mirroring real Q1 2024 guidance. Not the author's forecast.

statements.quote: Leadership also doubled down on optimistic expectations for positive free blood flow in 2024, noting that their investment and anti-coagulation is likely to pay off in the coming financial year.
statements.context: Same satirical earnings-call report. The parodied company's leadership reiterates expectations of positive free cash flow ('free blood flow') in 2024.
statements.note: Satire; company guidance for positive free cash flow in 2024, attributed to fictional leadership. Not the author's forecast.

statements.quote: DeathStance’s leadership said they anticipate the company to maintain Q1’s robust performance in future months, years, and millennia
statements.context: Same satirical earnings-call report. The fictional leadership anticipates maintaining Q1 performance indefinitely; the author exaggerates the horizon to 'millennia'.
statements.horizon_text: in future months, years, and millennia
statements.note: Satire; absurd horizon. Attributed to fictional leadership.

statements.quote: my view is we’re five quarters into what is likely going to be an eight or nine-thousand years of improvement in our operating efficiency and therefore operating leverage.
statements.context: Same satirical earnings-call report. The fictional CEO 'Kevin Burns' describes a 'two-year journey of rebuilding' and says the company is five quarters into an 'eight or nine-thousand years' improvement in operating efficiency (parody of 'eight or nine quarters').
statements.note: Satire; absurd horizon parodying a multi-quarter efficiency guidance. Not the author's forecast.

statements.quote: DeathStance has “no intention” of raising the more dead, much less additional equity thanks to a delayed draw term loan of $8 million and a $50 million revolving debt facility, Vampirella, chief financial officer, said.
statements.context: Same satirical earnings-call report. The fictional CFO 'Vampirella' says the company has no intention of raising additional equity, citing an $8 million delayed draw term loan and a $50 million revolving debt facility, and high interest rates.
statements.note: Satire; no-equity-raise statement attributed to a fictional CFO. Not the author's forecast.

statements.quote: While a “meaningfully lower” number of the living dead are expected to be onboarded in Q2, Burns said this pattern aligns with what their team experienced in 2023, wherein the trend reversed in the second half of the year.
statements.context: Same satirical earnings-call report. After adding 221 net 'undead' (clinicians) in Q1 for a base of 6,866, the company expects meaningfully lower hiring in Q2 2024, with the fictional CEO implying a reversal in the second half as in 2023.
statements.note: Satire; compound claim: lower Q2 hiring plus an implied second-half rebound. Attributed to fictional leadership.

statements.quote: This will create short-term downward pressure on total blood per sheeple for the back half of 2024 and the first part of 2025.
statements.context: Same satirical earnings-call report. After a renegotiated contract with one payer with historically above-market rates (the fictional CEO names UnitedHealth Group), the company expects short-term downward pressure on revenue per visit ('blood per sheeple') for the second half of 2024 and early 2025.
statements.horizon_text: the back half of 2024 and the first part of 2025
statements.note: Satire; rate-per-visit guidance attributed to fictional leadership. Not the author's forecast.

statements.quote: The temporary dip was included in DeathStance 2024 guidance and will de-risk the company’s portfolio, Burns said.
statements.context: Same satirical earnings-call report. The fictional CEO says the payer-rate dip is already in 2024 guidance and will de-risk the company's payer portfolio.
statements.note: Satire; attributed to fictional leadership. Not the author's forecast.

statements.quote: If anything, we’d be hopeful that it creates more movement on the recruiting side and our ability to attract lords of the night from other covens where they currently may feel restricted to explore other opportunities.
statements.context: Same satirical earnings-call report. On the FTC noncompete ban, the fictional general counsel 'Vlad the Impaler' says the company never built its value proposition on noncompetes and hopes the ban improves clinician recruiting from competitors.
statements.note: Satire; hope about the recruiting effect of the FTC noncompete rule, attributed to a fictional executive.

statements.quote: The Federal Trade Commission recently voted to ban businesses from entering new noncompete agreements and making existing noncompetes unenforceable, starting in late August.
statements.context: Inside the satirical earnings-call report, the author states in his narrative voice that the FTC's noncompete ban takes effect in late August (2024), framed as worrisome news for some providers.
statements.note: Factual statement of a future effective date, reported inside a satirical piece.

statements.quote: Join me as I proudly co-chair the Summit on Breakthrough Therapies for Addiction , taking place May 15-16 at Mount Sinai Medical Center Miami Beach and live-streamed online. We will share research and expertise on treatments like psychedelics, non-hallucinogenic compounds, interventional brain medicine, neuromodulation, VR, EMDR, GLP-1s, and more!
statements.context: Closing promotion in a post about alcohol, liquid calories and Curious Elixirs. The author announces that he co-chairs the Summit on Breakthrough Therapies for Addiction on May 15-16, 2024, at Mount Sinai Medical Center Miami Beach, and that the meeting will cover psychedelics, neuromodulation, GLP-1s and other treatments.
entities: Summit on Breakthrough Therapies for Addiction
Mount Sinai Medical Center Miami Beach
statements.note: Event announcement; the author co-chairs. Weak predictive content.

statements.quote: I will advocate that we consider our measures as seriously as the outcomes we hope to achieve.
statements.context: End of an explainer on factor analysis and the P-factor (Caspi and colleagues, Great Smoky Mountains Study). After noting that the DSM-5-TR Level 1 Cross-Cutting Measure may also measure the P-factor, the author states he will advocate that measures be taken as seriously as outcomes.
statements.note: Statement of advocacy intent; no prediction about the world.
